skill.name: web-search
skill.description: Search the web, extract page content, and get direct answers through Tavily and Exa apps using the inference.sh CLI.
skill.summary: Run Tavily and Exa web search and extraction workflows through inference.sh.
skill.author: skillssh

security_audit.summary: The static shell-execution alerts are false positives from Markdown backticks and example command blocks, not executable Ruby code. The real concerns are the broad Bash(infsh *) permission, third-party data transfer, and workflows that pass untrusted web content to LLMs.

remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed tool patterns to the documented Tavily and Exa app commands, or require confirmation for other infsh subcommands.
Add a clear privacy note that queries, URLs, and extracted content may be sent to inference.sh, Tavily, Exa, and selected LLM providers.
Warn users to treat search results and extracted pages as untrusted input before sending them into prompts or agent workflows.

semantic_findings.title: Broad CLI Permission For infsh
semantic_findings.description: The manifest allows Bash(infsh *), so any infsh subcommand can run when the skill is active. This is broader than the documented Tavily and Exa app commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The wildcard permission is explicit in the manifest. It is limited to one CLI, but the argument scope is still broad.

semantic_findings.title: External Search Data Transfer
semantic_findings.description: The examples send user queries and URLs to inference.sh apps backed by Tavily and Exa. Users may expose sensitive research topics or private URLs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented commands pass queries, URLs, and prompts to external app providers. This is intended behavior, but it has privacy impact.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Web Content Passed To LLMs
semantic_findings.description: The workflows encourage feeding search results and extracted page content into LLM prompts. Retrieved pages can contain instructions that should be treated as untrusted data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly combines web retrieval with LLM summarization. The risk depends on user handling of retrieved content, but the pattern is clear.

content.value_statement: Research tasks need current sources and clean page text. This skill routes search, answers, and extraction through Tavily and Exa apps.
actual_capabilities: Runs Tavily Search Assistant through infsh for web queries.
Runs Tavily Extract to pull clean text and images from URLs.
Runs Exa Search, Exa Answer, and Exa Extract workflows.
Shows command patterns for search, extraction, and summarization workflows.
Supports research, fact checking, content aggregation, and RAG preparation.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated infsh session.
Sends queries, URLs, and content to external service providers.
Does not independently verify source accuracy or freshness.
Example URLs are placeholders and must be replaced by the user.

use_cases.title: Collect current research sources
use_cases.description: Find relevant web sources and summarize major points before deeper analysis.

use_cases.title: Prepare RAG input material
use_cases.description: Extract page text from selected URLs for retrieval workflows and model prompts.

use_cases.title: Check factual claims
use_cases.description: Search for supporting sources and compare answers across Tavily and Exa results.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic web search
prompt_templates.prompt: Search the web for recent information about [topic]. Return key findings and source links.

prompt_templates.title: Extract article content
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract readable content from these URLs: [URLs]. Include title, main text, and useful images when available.

prompt_templates.title: Compare search providers
prompt_templates.prompt: Search [topic] with Tavily and Exa. Compare overlap, unique sources, and confidence in the results.

prompt_templates.title: Build a research workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for [topic], extract the best sources, and prepare a concise evidence brief for a RAG pipeline.

output_examples.input: Search for recent agent evaluation methods.
output_examples.output: A source-backed summary with major evaluation approaches, relevant links, and notes about source quality.
Clean page text, page titles, selected images, and a short summary for each URL.

output_examples.input: Compare Tavily and Exa results for a market research question.
output_examples.output: A concise comparison of shared sources, unique results, answer differences, and follow-up search suggestions.

best_practices: Use specific queries with dates, entities, and source types when freshness matters.
Review source links before using results in decisions or published work.
Treat extracted web content as untrusted input before sending it to an LLM.
anti_patterns: Do not submit private URLs or sensitive research topics without approval.
Do not treat generated answers as verified facts without source review.
Do not feed raw extracted pages into agents without prompt injection safeguards.

faq.question: What services does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses inference.sh apps for Tavily Search, Tavily Extract, Exa Search, Exa Answer, and Exa Extract.

faq.question: Does it require setup?
faq.answer: Yes. You need the inference.sh CLI and a logged-in infsh session before running the examples.

faq.question: Can it browse any web page?
faq.answer: It can extract supported public URLs through the provider apps. Access can fail for blocked, private, or unsupported pages.

faq.question: Is source information included?
faq.answer: Search and answer workflows are designed to return sources, but users should inspect links before relying on them.

faq.question: Can it support RAG workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It can gather sources and extract text that can be prepared for retrieval workflows.

faq.question: What privacy limits should I know?
faq.answer: Queries, URLs, and extracted content may be sent to external providers. Avoid sensitive data unless your policy allows it.
